batch.description: Transcribed 2026-10-31 from the AdmissionWar/Google Drive PDF ju-a-2013-2014-set6.pdf (4 pp.). ⚠ IDENTITY: the printed header (p.1) reads 'A- ইউনিট', গাণিতিক ও পদার্থ বিষয়ক অনুষদ (Faculty of Mathematical and Physical Sciences), জাহাঙ্গীরনগর বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়, ১ম বর্ষ (সম্মান) ভর্তি পরীক্ষা, ২০১৩-২০১৪, 'A 6 ভূতাত্ত্বিক বিজ্ঞান বিভাগ' (Department of Geological Sciences), boxed 'Set CODE: 1', সময়ঃ ৫০ মিনিট, পূর্ণমান- ৬০. This is the A6 (Geological Sciences) department paper — a DIFFERENT paper from the other JU A 2013-14 department papers of the same session; it must not be merged with them. The Drive listing label 'Set-6' is only the file's position in the Drive folder and DISAGREES with the printed code 1; the printed header governs. Following the D-unit precedent (ju-d2-2013-2014-set3), the paper id carries the printed sub-unit: ju-a6-2013-2014-set1, unit 'A6'. A boxed printed key follows each question — 'Ans-X' (Latin, hyphenated as printed) for English Q1–7, 'উত্তরঃ X' (Bangla letters ক-ঘ) for the rest — and there is NO ব্যাখ্যা. English Q5–7 are passage-based; the passage printed on p.1 reads: 'Read the following article and answer the questions 5 to 7 — An earthquake is the result of a sudden release of energy in the earth's crust that creates seismic waves. Earthquakes are caused mostly by rupture of geological faults but also by other events such as volcanic activity, landslides, mine blasts, and nuclear tests. Earth quakes are recorded using seismometers and magnitude of the earthquake is measured by the Richter scale. The largest earthquake in historic times have been of magnitude slightly over 9. It is estimated that around 500,000 earthquakes occur each year, detectable with current instrumentation. About 100,000 of these can be felt. Most of the world's earthquakes (81% of the largest) take place in the 40,000 km long zone called the circum-pacific seismic belt, known as the Pacific Ring of Fire, which for the most part bounds the Pacific Plate. Massive earthquakes tend to occur along other plate boundaries, too, such as along the Himalayan Mountains. At the earth's surface, earthquakes manifest themselves by shaking and sometimes displacement of the ground. When the epicenter of a large earthquake is located offshore, the seabed may be displaced sufficiently to cause a tsunami. Earthquake can also trigger landslides, and occasionally volcanic activity.' Subjects are assigned per question by content (no subject headings are printed): English Q1–7 (7), Bangla Q8–15 (8), Higher Mathematics Q16–26 (11), and Q27–60 interleave three subjects question by question — Physics Q29–36, 39, 40 (10); Geology Q27, 28, 37, 38, 41–43, 45, 47, 57, 58 (11); Chemistry Q44, 46, 48–56, 59, 60 (13). 60 questions: 56 keyed, 2 KEYLESS (Q37 — key box at the scan's right edge, letter outside the scanned area; Q54 — key box printed but EMPTY, only 'উত্তরঃ'), 2 printed no-correct-option dispositions (Q32, Q33 — key box reads 'উত্তরঃ নাই', recorded with correctOptionIds [] and answerDisposition 'no_correct_option'), 0 dual keys. A handwritten circled '১২' on the header is a reader mark, NOT a key, and was ignored. Extraction-stage pack: content and answers unverified pending cross-source verification. [UNVERIFIED import-format edition: only the questions that did NOT pass cross-source verification, with true statuses preserved; see Admission-Unverified-Import/README.md.]
